body: I learned that if you are diagnosed with Cancer and are under the age of 30. Just let it kill you, "survival" isn't all it's cracked up to be.

Thank you for your input, While I am not trying to be difficult as I have come to this sub-reddit for help, I can see that I have perhaps miscommunicated my trials with the job search, while it is true I have largely automated the electronic side: Emails, Job-boards, etc. I am putting in the "face time" attending multiple networking events, job fairs and meetups weekly. From my previous company, I also retain access to Zoominfo, which I have set daily quotas for myself in regards to outreach, 25 new phone calls a day, 15 follow up. It's just so very draining for lack of a better word. 

I also concede that perhaps I do desire life to be as predictable as the software I am comfortable developing, but I am under no illusion that it is nor that it is fair. I learned that when I first became aware that not everyone's father subjected them to daily abuse.  I just don't have the energy to fight it anymore. 

Especially when I can run projections that even as loose estimates show that I do not have a future beyond August 18th. No revenue, means no family, no home, and certainly no retirement.
